messages:
anya: Quick design sync 1: thinking about a horizontal role chip layout in the invite drawer. Idea: compact pills that expand inline to show permissions instead of a long list. Link to quick mock: https://figma.redwood/example :link:

matt: Chips would look cleaner but on narrow screens they may wrap weirdly. Proposal: show up to 3 pills inline, then a '+N more' overflow that opens the full list. Tooltip on truncated names. :thinking_face:

rui: Accessibility notes: each chip must be a focusable button. Use `role=button`, `aria-pressed` for selection state, and `aria-expanded` when it reveals details. When expanding inline, ensure `aria-live=polite` announcement like "Viewer role details expanded". Keyboard support: Enter/Space to toggle, Left/Right to move focus between chips.

anya: Good. Also UX decision: expand inline (push content) vs overlay. Inline keeps context; overlay avoids layout shifts. Which do we prefer for invite drawer?

matt: Lean inline accordion for discoverability. If we do inline, implement smooth scroll so expanded content is fully visible and focus moves into it. Add CSS to avoid page jump on mobile.

sarah: Copy suggestions if inline: chip label example: "Viewer 500>"); This will ensure full string isn't too long. For the confirmation language on SSO toggles: "Enable SSO enforcement for this org? Users who havent linked their SSO account will be blocked from signing in. To disable later, contact support." Might be too scary; legal may want exact wording.

ken: Telemetry: add events `invite_chips_open`, `invite_chip_select`, `invite_overflow_open`. Measure time from drawer open to invite sent. If overflow is used >50% on mobile, we should revisit the pattern.

anya: Accessibility nit: truncated chips need `aria-label` with full role + short summary, e.g., `aria-label=\"Viewer: can read projects, logs, and audit entries\"`. Also ensure focus ring is 4px wide in high-contrast mode.

rui: Audit log nav: if someone selects a role in the invite drawer and then goes to Audit Logs, preserve the selected role as a filter and show a clear pill: "Filter: Viewer (from Invite flow)" with an `x` to clear. Keyboard users should be able to press `Esc` to clear the filter when the filter pill has focus.

matt: For SSO-enabled orgs, annotate roles that require SSO with a lock icon and short tooltip: "SSO required to assign". Should we hide roles that are incompatible? I'd rather annotate than hide.

anya: About the SSO enforcement toggle: product suggests adding a typed-confirm for disabling enforcement. Draft modal copy: 
```
Title: Confirm disabling SSO enforcement
Body: Disabling SSO enforcement will allow accounts to sign in without your identity provider. To confirm, type your org name: <org-name>
Primary CTA: Confirm disable
Secondary CTA: Cancel
```

sarah: Small copy tweak: change "will allow accounts to sign in" to "may allow users to sign in without SSO" and make CTA: "Confirm disable (irreversible)" only if legal insists.

design-bot: design-assets: uploaded new component `invite/role-chips/v1` to Figma. Frames: mobile + desktop, overflow behavior. :white_check_mark:

anya: Next steps:
- Rui: produce keyboard/aria spec doc (due Thu EOD)
- Matt: add overflow behavior + responsive mock (Figma)
- Sarah: finalize SSO modal wording and run through legal
- Ken: create tracking tickets and add to invite epic

matt: ack :thumbsup:

rui: will include SR announcement examples and example DOM snippets :eyes:

sarah: looping in legal now.

ken: adding telemetry spike for this week.

anya: Thanks everyone 1 We'll validate with one accessibility engineer and ship a small A/B on mobile to measure overflow usage. :sparkles:
